title: The demo hub — Useful little worlds
thesis: Move the index from a utility directory toward an editorial collection while leaving room to find a more ownable visual expression.
summary: The first pass gave all 32 demos clearer hierarchy, search and category controls, richer previews, and a shared way home. The direction is useful; the look remains deliberately open for another pass.

comparisons.title: From app grid to editorial index
comparisons.caption: The revised hub makes the breadth of the collection easier to scan and gives several flagship demos their own small visual world, but its overall aesthetic is still being refined.

before.alt: The original Shipyard demo gallery with a straightforward header and grid of app cards.

after.alt: The Useful little worlds gallery with an oversized editorial headline, filters, and varied demo cards.

changes.title: The collection became navigable
changes.body: Search, category filters, live result counts, and responsive controls turn a long index into something visitors can actively browse.

changes.title: Flagships gained a preview
changes.body: Realm, Manifest, Fathom, Maelstrom, Flowforge, and Synth Studio received lightweight in-card scenes that suggest each experience before launch.

changes.title: Every demo gained a route home
changes.body: One shared, keyboard-accessible navigation control now connects the standalone demos back to the collection on desktop and mobile.

builderNote.quote: I like the direction, but not the look.
builderNote.context: Feedback on the first gallery-wide visual pass. The structure and intent are worth keeping; the visual language is not considered finished.

proof.label: Responsive crawl
proof.value: The hub and 31 canonical demos passed desktop and mobile checks

proof.label: Current state
proof.value: In revision, with the visual direction explicitly open

share.summary: A candid look at the Shipyard demo hub redesign: a stronger editorial direction whose visual expression is still in revision.
